phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength on the dermal field

paleobiology.chronoseries_note: Single Eusthenopteron time slice. No intraspecific predecessor or successor chronospecies.
paleobiology.formation: Escuminac Formation, Miguasha, Quebec (species); the vendored photograph is a Brussels mount of that species

equations.steady_state: u0 = a + b, v0 = b / (a + b)²
equations.jacobian: f_u = −1 + 2 u0 v0, f_v = u0², g_u = −2 u0 v0, g_v = −u0²
equations.turing_wavenumber: k_c² = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.boundary: Periodic Fourier domain on a flank patch; the museum photograph is a display mask, not a no-flux anatomical boundary

parameters.note: Time is rescaled by the reaction rate so the explicit Fourier step is stable. Spatial k_c is unchanged by that rescaling. These values are derived for λ = 104.2 µm and are not the 5.7 mm sibling slot.

chronoseries_delta.successor_relation: Next crownward elpistostegalian in the fin-to-limb series. Registry age 380 Ma is 1 Ma older than 379 Ma; the comparison used here is morphological, not a second Eusthenopteron chronospecies.
chronoseries_delta.quantity_that_changes: Mode count N = L / λ along the registry body length
chronoseries_delta.interpretation: At 104 µm the successor's longer body packs about 240 additional pigment wavelengths. The 5.7 mm organ-tier slot instead counts about 55 repeats of this same fundamental across one flank bar. Same species can carry both statements; the parameters are not shared.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion condition and critical wavenumber
Kondo & Asai 1995 and Nakamasu et al. 2009: living-fish dermal pigment cells form RD patterns
Andrews & Westoll 1970: postcranial skeleton of Eusthenopteron foordi
Species age 379 Ma and fin-to-limb placement as recorded in the project species registry
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameters with Dv/Du = 12 chosen so the formula k_c equals 2π per 104.2 µm
Fourier integration, dispersion-curve comparison, equal-diffusion control, autocatalysis ablation, Dv sweep
Body mask segmented from the Brussels photograph and used as a display domain for the ocellus field
transfer_boundary: Teleost chromatophore RD is applied to a Late Devonian tristichopterid dermis
104.2 µm is the assigned primordium-tier detail scale, identified with the model's selected wavelength, not a counted pore spacing on this slab
does_not_claim: That melanin stripes are preserved on the Miguasha or Brussels specimen
That the photograph contains a scale bar or a calibrated µm-per-pixel ratio
That Panderichthys or Tiktaalik have been measured at 104 µm in this study
